header:
Date: 2028-06-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Maya Thompson (Cascade - Head of ML); Rodrigo Alvarez (Cascade - Platform); Sana Iqbal (Cascade - Privacy); Ethan Cole (Cascade - Product); Chris (guest)
summary: Redwood demo of model catalog, benchmark interpretation, and compatibility matrix for Cascade Health triage workflow. Focus on picking open models that balance latency, cost, and safety. Discussed hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, routing policies, KV/prefix cache, and quantization. Agreed next steps to run bench on 3 candidate models and share SOC2/KMS docs.
topics: Overview of model catalog and filters
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna walk through how to pick models from the catalog focused on a triage flow, apologies if audio is a bit off for some folks.
[00:12] Maya Thompson: No worries, Alex. Quick context: we run a rule-based triage then a short LLM step to summarize symptoms for clinicians, 1-1.5k tokens usually. Latency target is sub-400ms p50 ideally.
[00:28] Priya Nair: Got it. We'll show the catalog filters, bench numbers, and then a compatibility matrix for on-prem/private options.
[00:37] Rodrigo Alvarez: Important: we need KMS integration, regional residency for EU data, and audit logs.
[00:44] Alex: Yep, we'll surface those. Quick housekeeping: call recorded. Starting with catalog — top-left you can filter by family, seq len, quantization friendly, and safety profile.
[01:10] Priya: (screen) here's our open-model list. Note the compat scores on the right — that's runtime fuzz, kernel match, and quantization tolerance combined. The matrix highlights models that hit our latency band on A100 and on Ampere.
[01:35] Chris: (murmur) that's cool.
[01:41] Maya: How reliable are those compat scores? Are they from live runs or heuristics?
[01:48] Priya: They're hybrid — heuristic mapping from model arch + kernel table, plus sampled bench results. We tag confidence low/med/high. For new community models confidence might be medium.
[02:05] Alex: For a production pick you want high confidence and a bench-run on a representative prompt set. That's why we recommend the 3-model bench.
[02:18] Ethan Cole: We have safety constraints — can't generate PHI or free text that reveals PII. How does the catalog show safety?
[02:27] Priya: Each model has a safety filter note — shows hallucination tendency and red-team tag if models failed certain tests. We also have a reranking/tool-calling suggestion for stricter outputs.
[02:41] Rodrigo: On infra: we may go private VPC initially. Does the console show a private catalog or is it the same?
[02:49] Alex: Same API surface. Private deployment uses a separate control plane but your catalog can be curated; you can pin allowed models. The Console shows a "Private Catalog" toggle and policy bindings.
[03:05] Maya: Show us the benchmark matrix for our use-case.
[03:08] Priya: Sure. (screen) here's a bench matrix — rows are models, columns are p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens with quantized vs full fp32 runs. For short contexts quantized runs sometimes win on cost with small latency hit.
[03:25] Maya: Which models meet sub-400ms p50 on our sample?
[03:29] Priya: On T4-style instances only a couple; on A10/A100 more options. For 1-1.5k tokens we flagged Model-X-lite, LM-Compact-13B-q4 and OpenTriage-7B as candidate picks. Note: Model names in our catalog are normalized; sometimes upstream names differ.
[03:52] Maya: The OpenTriage-7B — does that have a safety red-team pass?
[03:57] Priya: Medium safety confidence, passed our red-team prompts with moderate guardrails. We recommended applying output filters and a reranker.
[04:10] Rodrigo: If we do Dedicated GPUs vs Hosted, what's the latency delta typically?
[04:15] Alex: Dedicated gives more predictable tail behavior because you control pooling and concurrency; hosted is bursty but lower ops for small customers. In our tests Dedicated on Ampere with optimized kernels reduces p95 by 30-40% over shared hosted in high concurrency.
[04:36] Rodrigo: OK. Also need to know if runtime supports KV cache sharing across replicas for chat-like flows.
[04:42] Priya: Yes, KV cache management is supported. We have documentation on prefix caching, eviction policies and how caching interacts with batching. For triage you might get 2-3x token cost savings if you reuse prefixes.
[05:00] Sana Iqbal: On the compliance side, we need encryption at rest with our KMS, HSM optional, and full audit logs. Is there a sample integration doc?
[05:10] Alex: We'll share SOC2 and KMS integration notes; Redwood Private supports customer KMS via IAM and HSM-backed keys for on-prem.
[05:20] Priya: Also note the Console exposes per-token cost breakdown by model and route, which helps you tag the triage route separately.
[05:32] Maya: About routing and fallback — if we pick OpenTriage-7B but it's not available, what does Redwood do?
[05:40] Priya: You can configure routing policy: strict, relaxed, or cost-prioritized. In relaxed mode it will fallback to a compatible model family and optionally apply heavier reranking. We log fallbacks and you can set alerts.
[05:55] Ethan: Can we set different rollouts per env? dev vs prod?
[05:59] Alex: Yes, rollouts and canary deployments per environment. You can also bind model pin by route.
[06:08] Rodrigo: For benching, what inputs do you need? We'll provide 50 representative prompts and 2k concurrent request pattern?
[06:16] Priya: 50-200 prompts is perfect; include token distribution. We'll run p50/p95 and cost estimates at 1k qps and a 10qps baseline — basically mimic your traffic.
[06:28] Maya: One thing: our triage sometimes requires tool calling to fetch patient vitals from a redacted store. Any constraints?
[06:36] Priya: Tool calling is supported; in Private you can wire to internal endpoints. We recommend a validation layer to strip PHI in transit.
[06:44] Alex: Quick demo of the Console Optimize tab — it suggests batching sizes, quant profiles, and shows estimated cost delta.
[06:51] Priya: (screen) here's a model page for LM-Compact-13B-q4: kernel map shows which kernels on Ampere and A100 we hit, and a compatibility hint for fused attention. Sometimes the parser transcribes fused attention as "fussed" — sorry — but basically it's an optimization.
[07:08] Maya: Good. How about vector DB embeddings mismatch risk? We plan to embed triage summaries.
[07:15] Priya: The Console tags embedding model stability and suggests retraining frequency. For short summaries you might use a smaller embedder to save cost.
[07:26] Ethan: Pricing — rough per 1k token for these models?
[07:30] Alex: We'll send precise tiers; ballpark: small open 7B quantized ~ $0.03/1k tokens on Hosted, 13B quantized ~ $0.08/1k; Dedicated lowers base unit cost depending on commit. We'll include a sample Dedicated amortization.
[07:47] Rodrigo: Anything special about quantization—will q4 lead to accuracy regressions on medical terms?
[07:53] Priya: It can. We recommend running quality evals alongside perf benches. Optimize has a reg check that runs your eval set and flags any per-prompt degradations.
[08:05] Maya: Let's step through a sample bench output.
[08:08] Priya: (screen) here's the CSV we produce — model, instance type, p50, p95, cost, tokens/sec, reg-quality score. For example OpenTriage-7B on A10: p50 320ms, p95 680ms, cost $0.027/1k, quality 0.87 vs baseline.
[08:30] Maya: That p95 is high. Is that due to cold starts?
[08:34] Priya: Likely—can optimize with warm pooling, reduce concurrency per worker, or pick Dedicated. Also batching strategy affects shot noise.
[08:44] Ethan: For the pilot, what would you recommend?
[08:47] Alex: Start with hosted benching on your prompts, run 3-model shortlist with Optimize's suggestions, then a 2-week Dedicated pilot if performance needs stabilization. For privacy-critical flows, do a Private pilot in a VPC.
[09:02] Rodrigo: Timeline-wise we want pilot running end of June. Is that feasible?
[09:06] Alex: Yes, if we get prompts and infra constraints this week. Priya can spin bench harness.
[09:12] Priya: I'll need the 50 prompts, expected concurrency profile, and a sample API key placeholder. We'll run the bench and share spreadsheets.
[09:21] Sana: Also we need legal SOW details for Private deployment and data processing addendum.
[09:26] Alex: We'll loop in legal and share a template SOW; Alex will own that.
[09:31] Ethan: One more question: can we lock model versions in production to ensure reproducible outputs?
[09:35] Priya: Yes, we have model version pinning and rollout tracking in Console, with diffs for model weights/quantization changes.
[09:45] Chris: (soft) does Redwood do auto-quant?
[09:48] Priya: We suggest quant profiles but we don't auto-quantize upstream models without consent — you can apply Redwood-managed quant profiles in Dedicated/Private.
[09:58] Maya: Show me the compatibility matrix for our infra.
[10:01] Priya: (screen) matrix rows are models, columns are features: VPC deploy, KMS support, kernel match A100, Ampere, fused kernels, quant friendly, safety pass. Green means good. OpenTriage-7B is green except for high confidence on safety.
[10:20] Rodrigo: How do we enable audit logs for tenants?
[10:24] Alex: In Console -> Security -> Audit Logs. You can stream logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud forwarder; Private supports on-prem log sinks.
[10:34] Sana: Any certifications for cloud-hosted offering?
[10:37] Alex: We maintain SOC2 Type II and provide ISO docs on request for enterprise.
[10:44] Maya: Ok can we summarize decisions and owners?
[10:49] Alex: Sure. Shortlist: OpenTriage-7B, LM-Compact-13B-q4, Model-X-lite. Bench: Redwood runs bench and returns CSV. Compliance: Redwood to send SOC2/KMS docs. Pilot: 2-week pilot for Dedicated or Private depending on bench.
[11:05] Priya: I'll also provide a sample routing policy that uses strict for PHI paths and relaxed for generic summaries.
[11:14] Maya: Great. Any questions from your side?
[11:18] Rodrigo: Implementation detail — how do we run pilot on-prem? We have an internal GPU cluster with RDMA.
[11:24] Priya: Private supports on-prem packaging; for RDMA we recommend specific kernel flags and box-level tuning — we'll share a runbook. It may require a small agent install.
[11:36] Ethan: For the evals, what's your scoring metric suggestion? We were thinking ROUGE + clinician adjudication.
[11:44] Priya: ROUGE + human-in-the-loop is good; Optimize supports automated per-prompt diffs and flags regressions beyond a threshold.
[11:55] Maya: Ok — last thing, can you include cost projection for 100k summaries/month across the three models?
[12:02] Alex: We'll include that in the bench spreadsheet; it's one of the export columns.
[12:10] (longer silence/typing)
[12:28] Alex: cool. We'll follow up with docs and timeline. Thanks everyone.
[12:35] Maya: Thanks, bye.
[12:38] End of recording.

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcripts around kernel names and fused attention, speaker overlaps, and filler words preserved. The transcript above is an extract; full bench CSV and Console screenshots referenced during call and to be shared in follow-up.
